jobs.title: Nine Years · before
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 26, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; GULLY — aged 27, stocky man with a round face, thick forearms, sleeves pushed up; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. GULLY usually wears backwards cap, red plaid flannel; the uncle's black rubber apron over it only behind the counter. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: The day before the ninth September 12: the corn bought, on the counter in its husks, and Gully asking whether Wood wants it grilled or boiled this year. Same as always, Wood says. Gully says he has to ask; it's the job. Panel 1: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, ears of corn in their husks on a shop counter with a stocky man in an apron and a thin man on a stool (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Gully says "Grilled or boiled.". Panel 2: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man on a stool answering without looking up (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "Same as always.". Panel 3: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a stocky man in an apron shrugging behind a counter (in this panel: GULLY). Gully says "I have to ask. It's the job.". Panel 4: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a small dog on a shop floor gazing up at ears of corn on a counter (in this panel: BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_27 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @gully_27 for the character the strip's Gully at 23-31; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31.
